8.en: When using these rules, the party always has a Subtlety Rating ranging between a minimum of 1 and a maximum of 10. The party’s Subtlety Rating determines their Subtlety Level, each of which has different mechanical effects on their investigations. The GM sets the party’s initial Subtlety at the beginning of a mission based on how aware people and organisations are of their presence in their area of operations. Most investigations begin within @UUID[.k3IIBps2ZS9Ap23D#covert-(subtlety-10-8)]{Covert Subtlety (10—8)} unless the local population is suspicious before the party arrives. After that, their Subtlety Rating fluctuates based on the party’s actions and decisions during their missions.

12.en: Generally, higher Subtlety means people in the area know relatively little about the party’s identity, allegiances, activities, and motivations. This allows them to act clandestinely without hindrance but makes invoking the Inquisition’s reputation harder. Lower Subtlety represents greater public awareness and suspicion, eliciting paranoia, worry, compliance, and obedience amongst the populace and more violent or evasive manoeuvres from their enemies. Subtlety is tracked across 4 Subtlety Levels to represent these effects, each with narrative and mechanical consequences.

16.en: Each level of Subtlety has advantages and disadvantages, so no single level is necessarily better than another; the most advantageous Subtlety level in any situation depends on what the party is trying to accomplish, the party’s approach and the surrounding circumstances involved.
